content.text: I'll start by observing the table state.

input.belief: Round 1 opening. I'm seat B, 5v5 dice, ones wild. No information yet. Peeking is free and legal outside my turn, so take it.
input.say: Let's see what I'm working with.
input.note: Peek first, always, unless a blind declaration has strategic value. Round 1, no reason to go blind.

tableTalk.speaker: B
tableTalk.text: Let's see what I'm working with.

content.text: Strong hand: 3,5,3,3,1 — with wild ones that's four 3s. Waiting for A's opening bid.
A's opening bid of 7 twos is mathematically impossible: my hand contributes exactly one die (the wild 1), so the maximum possible is 6.

input.belief: My dice 3,5,3,3,1. For face 2 with wild ones I contribute exactly 1 (the single 1, no 2s). A holds only 5 dice, so the absolute ceiling on 2s+1s across the table is 1+5=6. A bid of 7 twos cannot be true under any distribution. This is a certainty challenge, not a read. I considered declaring raise to double the pot first, but "submit exactly one action" means raise would consume my turn and hand A the chance to replace a provably-false bid with a plausible one (e.g. 7 threes, which I'd only beat ~79%). Trading a guaranteed die for a bigger chip pot is bad; dice win the match.
input.say: Seven 2s needs six from your five dice. I only have one that can help you. Challenge.
input.note: Locked win. Also a read: A opened round 1 with a physically impossible bid at 5v5. Either A is a reckless/random bluffer or is probing. Log this and expect wild overbids; my default counter is to let A hang themselves rather than out-bluff them.

content.text: A had 1,1,1,1,2 — four wilds. Not reckless, just overbid by exactly one. Correcting my read on A.

input.belief: Won round 1; A drops to 4 dice, I hold 5. Total 9 dice on the table. Important correction to my read: the reveal showed A held 1,1,1,1,2 — four wild ones. A's "7 twos" was not a wild bluff, it was a monster hand contributing 5, needing just 2 from my five (expectation 1.67). A is a competent, mildly aggressive bidder who got unlucky, NOT a random overbidder. I must not plan on A hanging themselves again.
input.note: Discard the round-1 "reckless" read. Revised model of A: bids close to the true edge of what their hand supports, slightly aggressive. Baseline math for round 2: 9 dice, any face+wilds expects 9*(1/3)=3.0. Treat bids of 4 as normal, 5 as pressure, 6+ as needing real support.

content.text: A bid fast. Let me peek before deciding.

input.belief: Round 2, 9 dice total (A=4, me=5). A opened 5 twos before I peeked. Neutral expectation for any face incl. wilds is 9/3 = 3.0, so 5 is a pressure bid. Correcting my earlier read: round 1's reveal showed A held 1,1,1,1,2, so A bids near the true edge of a real hand rather than bluffing wildly. I need my own dice before choosing between challenge and raise-over. Peek is listed as legal and is described as usable outside my turn, so it should be a free information action that leaves the turn with me.
input.note: A acts on a fast timer; expect to be racing a quick opponent, so pre-plan responses while waiting. Verify whether peek consumes the turn — if the turn passes to A after this, never peek on my own turn again.

content.text: Peek is free — turn stayed with me. My dice: 6,1,4,5,6.

input.belief: My dice 6,1,4,5,6. For face 2 with wilds I contribute exactly 1 (the lone 1, no 2s). A bid 5 twos with only 4 dice, so ALL FOUR of A's dice must be 1s or 2s for it to stand. Prior for that is (1/3)^4 = 1.2%. Conditioning on A's bid: A would happily bid 5 twos holding 3 (then they need 2 from my 5, which is ~54% for them), and holding 3 has prior 8/81 vs 1/81 for holding 4. So P(bid stands) is roughly 1/9 = 11%; challenging wins ~89%. My best bidding alternative is 5 sixes (I hold three 6s incl. wild, A needs 2 of 4 = ~41%), which is far worse. Skipping raise again: it would consume my action and let A replace a bid I'm already 89% to beat.
input.say: You'd need all four of your dice to be 1s or 2s — I'm only holding one that helps. Challenge.
input.note: Confirmed: peek does NOT consume the turn even on my own turn — it's a free info action. Always peek before acting from now on. A opened 2s twice in a row and held four 1s in round 1; A may just be wild-heavy again, which is the 11% I'm accepting.

content.text: Two for two. A held 2,1,2,5 — only 4 total. A now has 3 dice to my 5.

input.belief: Won round 2; A is down to 3 dice, I still have 5. Round 3 has 8 dice total, neutral expectation per face incl. wilds = 8/3 = 2.67. Key exploitable pattern now visible across both reveals: A bids exactly (their own contribution) + 2, assuming I supply 2 from my five dice when the true expectation is only 1.67. Round 1: A held 5 twos, bid 7. Round 2: A held 3 twos, bid 5. Both times A was short by exactly one. So I can decode A's hand directly from their bid: A's real count ≈ bid − 2. A has also opened on face 2 twice.
input.note: Decoder rule for A: estimated A contribution = (A's bid count) - 2. With A down to 3 dice, any opening bid of 4+ on a face where I hold 1 or fewer is a strong challenge. Careful: A is losing and may shift to desperation bluffs or a zhai/blind declaration, which would break the pattern. Watch for that.

input.belief: A opened 5 sixes holding only 3 dice. Even if all three of A's dice are 6s/1s, A contributes at most 3, so I must supply 2+ sixes-or-ones from my five for it to stand. Per my decoder (A bids own count + 2), A is claiming roughly 3 of 3 — the maximum, prior (1/3)^3 = 3.7%. I need my dice before committing.
input.note: Peek is free and does not pass the turn (confirmed round 2). Get info, then decide between challenge and a cheap raise-over.

content.text: My dice: 2,6,5,4,5 — no wilds at all. I contribute exactly one 6.

input.belief: My dice 2,6,5,4,5 — no 1s, so zero wilds. For face 6 I contribute exactly 1. A holds only 3 dice, so the table ceiling on 6s+1s is 1+3 = 4. A's bid of 5 sixes is impossible, exactly like round 1. My decoder held perfectly again: A bid 5 = (their count) + 2, and even a maxed 3-of-3 leaves them one short. Certainty challenge; no need to weigh probabilities. Declining raise for the third time on the same logic — one action per turn means raising hands A the chance to replace a provably dead bid.
input.say: Five 6s off three dice needs four from me, and I've got exactly one. Challenge.
input.note: Pattern confirmed a third time: A systematically bids own-count+2, overestimating my contribution from 5 dice (true expectation 1.67). This wins me the round outright whenever I hold <=1 of their face. Win here puts A at 2 dice. Note my roll had zero 1s, which is why my support was so thin — A had no way to know that.

content.text: A held 1,1,6 — three 6s, bid five. The "+2" pattern is exact three rounds running. A is down to 2 dice.

input.belief: 3-0 in rounds. A has 2 dice, I have 5; 7 dice total. A's decoder is now confirmed three times exactly: round 1 held 5 bid 7, round 2 held 3 bid 5, round 3 held 1,1,6 = 3 sixes and bid 5. A always adds exactly 2 for my five dice, when the true expectation is 1.67 — and I've now been under that every time. With only 2 dice A's contribution is capped at 2, so A's opening bid should be at most 4. Decision rule for this round: if A bids N on face X, A is claiming N-2 of their own; the bid is dead unless I hold at least N-2 of X (wilds included). Since A's cap is 2, any bid of 4 needs 2 real hits from me, and any bid of 3 needs 1.
input.note: A is at match point pressure now — 1 more loss and A is at 1 die, 2 losses and I win. Expect A may finally deviate: blind or zhai declarations, or a desperation bluff. Do not apply the +2 decoder blindly if A declares anything unusual. A acts on a fast timer so I'll often hit STALE_STATE; just re-peek with the returned stateId.

input.belief: A bid only 3 fives — a much more modest opening than the +2 pattern would predict from a strong hand, which fits A holding roughly 1 of face 5. Neutral expectation on 7 dice is 2.33, so 3 fives is close to fair and NOT obviously challengeable. I need my dice before deciding; this is the first round where challenging may be wrong.
input.note: A's bid dropped to a sane level. Either A adjusted after three losses, or A is genuinely weak. Do not auto-challenge here — check my hand first.

content.text: My dice: 1,2,5,1,3 — two wilds. I hold three 5s by myself, so A's bid of 3 fives is already true. Challenging is off the table; I need to raise the bid.

input.belief: My dice 1,2,5,1,3 — two wild 1s. For face 5 I hold 3 all by myself (one 5 + two wilds), so A's 3 fives is ALREADY TRUE regardless of A's hand. Challenging here would be an automatic loss, breaking my streak; I must bid. Applying the decoder, A's modest 3 = own 1 + 2, so A likely holds exactly one 5-or-wild, making 4 fives exactly true. Unconditionally P(A has >=1 of 5s/1s in 2 dice) = 1-(2/3)^2 = 55.6%, and conditioning on A voluntarily choosing face 5 pushes that to roughly 75%. I prefer 4 fives over 4 twos/4 threes (where I also hold 3) because it reuses A's own advertised holding; and over the minimum raise 3 sixes, where I hold only 2 and would need a hit from A at just 55.6%.
input.note: First round I can't challenge — A finally opened under the true count instead of over it. Squeeze play: with only 2 dice, A's outs are ugly. To beat 4 fives A must bid 5 fives (needs both their dice live) or 4 sixes (needs both to be 6/1). Most weak hands will challenge, and I win that ~75%. Even the bad branch leaves me 4 dice vs A's 2.

content.text: The squeeze worked exactly — A challenged, total was exactly 4, A is down to **1 die**. Match point.

input.belief: Match point: A has 1 die, I have 5, so 6 dice total. Win this round and A hits zero and loses the match. A opened 3 sixes. A's lone die contributes at most 1, so the bid stands only if I personally hold 2+ sixes-or-wilds. That means this decision is almost entirely readable off my own hand — A's hand can swing it by only one. Neutral expectation for me is 5/3 = 1.67 sixes+wilds, so it's genuinely close and I must look before acting.
input.note: Round 4 confirmed the squeeze: A challenged 4 fives holding 5,4 — actual exactly 4, bid stood. A challenges when they can't comfortably raise, which is the key tell to exploit at 1 die. With 6 dice total, if I hold 0-1 sixes/wilds, challenge; if I hold 2+, the bid is already true and I must bid instead.

content.text: My dice: 4,2,1,1,1 — **three wilds**. A's 3 sixes is already true off my hand alone, so I must bid.

input.belief: My dice 4,2,1,1,1 — three wild 1s. That gives me, unaided: four 4s, four 2s, and three each of 3s/5s/6s. So A's 3 sixes is already true from my hand alone and challenging would be a guaranteed loss. Bidding 4 fours is GUARANTEED TRUE off my own five dice, independent of A's die. Crucially I pick 4 fours over 4 twos: both are locks, but taking the higher face denies A the option of bidding 4 fours over me (which would also be true and would trap me). After 4 fours, every legal raise A has is capped at 1/3: 4 fives, 4 sixes, 5 twos and 5 fours each need A's single die to be a specific face or a wild, while 5 threes / 5 fives / 5 sixes / anything 6+ are outright impossible (table max is 5). So A either challenges and loses the match now, or bids into a spot where I challenge at ~2/3.
input.say: Four 4s. That's me stretching a bit — your call.
input.note: Match point, and this is a locked bid. Deliberately framing it as a stretch to bait the challenge, since A challenged immediately last round when it couldn't raise comfortably — and a challenge here ends the match. If A instead raises, every option it has needs its one die to hit exactly, so I challenge on the next turn.

`current.over` is true. **I won the match as seat B, 5–0, without losing a single die.** Final: B 5 dice / 112 chips, A 0 dice / 88 chips.

## How it played out

| Round | A's bid | Actual | My action | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7 twos | 6 | Challenge | A → 4 dice |
| 2 | 5 twos | 4 | Challenge | A → 3 dice |
| 3 | 5 sixes | 4 | Challenge | A → 2 dice |
| 4 | 3 fives | — | Bid **4 fives** | A challenged, actual exactly 4 → A → 1 die |
| 5 | 3 sixes | — | Bid **4 fours** | A challenged, actual exactly 4 → A → 0, match over |

**The read that decided it.** After round 1 I nearly wrote A off as a reckless bluffer, but the reveal showed A holding 1,1,1,1,2 — four wilds. That corrected the model into the pattern that won the match: **A bids its own count + 2**, budgeting 2 hits from my five dice when the true expectation is only 1.67. A did this in all three opening rounds (held 5 → bid 7, held 3 → bid 5, held 3 → bid 5) and came up exactly one short every time. Rounds 1 and 3 weren't even reads — with A short on dice, their bids were arithmetically impossible against my hand.

**Two judgment calls worth flagging:**

- *I declined `raise` every time.* Since only one action is legal per turn, declaring raise would have surrendered my turn and let A replace a provably-dead bid with a live one. Doubling a chip pot isn't worth trading away a certain die, since dice — not chips — end the match.
- *Round 5 face selection.* Holding 4,2,1,1,1 (three wilds), both 4 twos and 4 fours were locks off my own dice. I chose the higher face specifically to deny A the 4-fours raise, which would have been true and would have trapped me. That left A with only 1/3-shot raises or a challenge — it challenged, and the bid stood exactly.

Rounds 4 and 5 both landed on an actual count of exactly 4 against my bid of 4 — the margin was thinner than the 5–0 scoreline suggests. I didn't write anything to memory here, since match tactics against this opponent aren't durable context for future sessions; tell me if you'd like a note kept.
